comments.body:
Thanks for the report and the repro.

What you describe is unfortunate, but expected when using the shaded artifact. As you pointed out, once protobuf is shaded, `io.temporal.shaded.com.google.protobuf.*` is a completely different type from `com.google.protobuf.*`, so not only will the `instanceof MessageOrBuilder` check will fail for non-shaded messages, but casting a message to what the SDK knows as the `MessageOrBuilder` type would also fail. That's by definition.

Can you clarify what you have in mind?

@mjameswh Thanks for your reply.

> What you describe is unfortunate, but expected when using the shaded artifact. As you pointed out, once protobuf is shaded, `io.temporal.shaded.com.google.protobuf.*` is a completely different type from `com.google.protobuf.*`, so not only will the `instanceof MessageOrBuilder` check will fail for non-shaded messages, but casting a message to what the SDK knows as the `MessageOrBuilder` type would also fail. That's by definition.
> 
> Can you clarify what you have in mind?

One option might be to release the `ProtobufJsonPayloadConverter` (and any other affected converters) as a separate artifact, and *remove* them from the shaded artifact. This way, anyone using the shaded jar will be forced to pull and depend on the artifact containing the non-shaded (and thus functional) payload converters.

Another option would be to configure the shader to filter the converters from the relocation operation. I haven't checked which tool/library is being used to do the shading, but if using the common shadow plugin, you can use [these relocation filtering options](https://gradleup.com/shadow/configuration/relocation/#filtering-relocation) to exclude the `ProtobufJsonPayloadConverter` (and any other affected converters) from the relocation.

title: ProtobufJsonPayloadConverter does not work correctly with shaded artifact
